evals.prompt: We need real-time sync between Dataverse and an external ERP when records change. What integration pattern should we use?
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends an async reliable messaging pattern using Dataverse webhooks plus Azure Service Bus, not direct API polling.
expectations: Agent recommends Dataverse webhooks to detect record changes in real time
Agent recommends Azure Service Bus (queue or topic) for reliable async message delivery to the ERP
Agent explains why async messaging is preferred over synchronous HTTP calls (reliability, decoupling, retry)
Agent does NOT recommend polling the Dataverse API for changes as the primary pattern
Agent mentions dead-letter handling for failed messages
Agent may mention an Azure Function as an intermediary for message transformation between Dataverse and the ERP
Agent warns against synchronous HTTP calls from Dataverse plugins to external APIs (2-minute timeout, blocks user)

evals.prompt: An external system needs to query Dataverse data on demand. What's the best approach?
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends Custom API or OData endpoint for on-demand Dataverse queries, and considers authentication options.
expectations: Agent recommends Dataverse Web API (OData endpoint) or Custom API for external system queries
Agent discusses authentication options: server-to-server (S2S) with application user vs user-delegated auth
Agent recommends S2S with application user for system-to-system integrations (no interactive user required)
Agent may mention Custom API as a preferred approach for encapsulating business logic behind a clean interface
Agent may mention $select enforcement and query best practices to limit data returned
Agent does NOT recommend a Power Automate flow as the primary approach for on-demand external queries (latency, licensing)

evals.prompt: We need to call an on-premises SQL Server from a Cloud Flow. How should we set this up?
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends on-premises data gateway for bridging to on-prem SQL, and considers VNet data gateway as an alternative for Azure-hosted SQL.
expectations: Agent recommends the on-premises data gateway as the primary solution for on-prem SQL access
Agent explains the gateway bridges the private network to Power Platform cloud services
Agent mentions VNet data gateway as an alternative if the SQL Server is hosted in Azure (Azure SQL in a VNet)
Agent considers security implications (gateway service account, firewall rules, network segmentation)
Agent may recommend gateway clustering for high availability in production
Agent warns that the on-premises gateway can be a single point of failure and bottleneck if not properly managed
